fullPassage: Imagine you're trying to decide which of three laptops to purchase online. The first has many reviews and a high rating; the second has fewer reviews and a low rating; and the third has no reviews at all. Chances are that you will select the one with the most satisfied customers. This is due to something called social proof, a psychological phenomenon based on the idea that people strive to conform to social norms. Marketers use it to more or less borrow third-party influence in the interest of luring new customers. Shoppers who are undecided about which product to buy are easily swayed by the reviews and recommendations of other people who have bought the items they are considering. This is why companies are so eager to persuade their customers to leave reviews—the social proof they create is an invaluable selling point.
